assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational and unusually consequential body of political-economy research linking political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives, and fiscal policy.
assessment.attribution: Persson, Besley, and Tabellini are central contributors to the theoretical and empirical development represented by this broad contribution.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped research across political economy and public economics over several decades and has clear relevance for long-run development.
uncertainties: The breadth of the proposed contribution makes a sharply bounded prize citation challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research has transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and its connection to place and policy.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are highly identifiable leaders in building and applying this empirical research program.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a substantial, influential literature and is sufficiently mature for assessment.
uncertainties: The contribution is comparatively recent and its full policy interpretation remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence methods supplied compelling evidence on discrimination and materially changed empirical labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are particularly closely associated with landmark experimental evidence; Charles is an important contributor to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been replicated, extended internationally, and remain central to evidence on labour-market discrimination.
uncertainties: Attribution across the wider experimental discrimination literature is necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection became a core framework for understanding trade, productivity, and the distributional effects of globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the indispensable originator of the canonical framework, with Helpman and Redding major contributors to its development and application.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply embedded in modern trade research and has been tested in extensive firm-level work.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit among the several related trade-modeling contributions is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life health, shocks, and skill formation has established the long-term economic importance of childhood conditions.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha each made distinctive and complementary contributions to the empirical and dynamic foundations of the field.
assessment.maturity: Findings have accumulated across settings and influenced both economics and public-policy research.
uncertainties: The candidate combines related empirical and theoretical strands rather than one single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification provided a fundamental alternative to unwarranted point identification and improved the credibility of empirical inference.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the defining intellectual figure, while Tamer and Molinari made major contributions to moment inequalities and implementation.
assessment.maturity: The methods are established across econometrics and applied work, with enduring implications for transparent assumptions.
uncertainties: Its broad methodological impact can be less visible than that of more directly policy-facing contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework offered a powerful account of productivity gaps and cross-country income differences using distortions in resource allocation.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow, and Restuccia are prominent and appropriately connected contributors to the central framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach has produced a large literature and remains influential in research on growth and development.
uncertainties: Empirical measurement of distortions and causal interpretation remain subjects of active debate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work advanced rigorous economic treatment of exhaustible resources, natural capital, biodiversity, and sustainability.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central figures in the analytical foundations of this research area.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is longstanding and increasingly important as environmental constraints enter economic policy and national accounting.
uncertainties: The broad environmental-economics citation encompasses several distinct lines of work and difficult valuation questions.
